distillation_scope.case_source_policy: Disease-only distillation from the disease name and project schema/axis registry. No real case reports or disease-specific case JSONs for this leaf were read or used.
distillation_scope.leaf_granularity: First-layer disease manifold for infection and inflammation involving chorion, amnion, amniotic fluid, placenta, decidua, fetus, or a clinically linked combination. Organism class, rupture-of-membranes timing, gestational age, preterm labor, fetal status, neonatal exposure, maternal sepsis, postpartum extension, delivery route, and antibiotic susceptibility are represented as axes, risk modifiers, treatment modifiers, event hazards, or future subtype layers rather than extra disease-name qualifiers.
distillation_scope.boundary_policy: This leaf is distinct from postpartum endometritis, septic abortion, preterm labor without infection, isolated epidural-related fever, pyelonephritis, appendicitis, placental abruption, amniotic fluid embolism, and neonatal sepsis as standalone leaves. Shared fever, tachycardia, uterine tenderness, sepsis, fetal distress, and postpartum infection axes should be consumed without double-counting when vector-field superposition is used.
distillation_scope.ontology_note: The core manifold is ascending or less commonly hematogenous intra-amniotic microbial/inflammatory activity, maternal systemic inflammation, fetal inflammatory response, labor/membrane activation, and source-control dependence on effective antimicrobial exposure plus delivery. Diagnostic summary labels are avoided; microbiology, amniotic fluid, maternal, fetal, labor, postpartum, and treatment-context axes carry the evidence.

latent_mechanisms.display_name: 上行性多菌種侵入 / Ascending polymicrobial inoculation
latent_mechanisms.clinical_meaning: Vaginal or cervical organisms ascend across ruptured or intact membranes into decidua, membranes, or amniotic fluid; less commonly hematogenous organisms seed the compartment.

latent_mechanisms.display_name: 脱落膜・絨毛膜羊膜炎症 / Decidual and chorioamniotic inflammation
latent_mechanisms.clinical_meaning: Neutrophilic and cytokine-rich inflammation of decidua, chorion, amnion, and placental membranes, producing uterine tenderness, purulent or malodorous fluid, and placental histologic inflammation.

latent_mechanisms.display_name: 羊水内感染活動性 / Amniotic fluid infection activity
latent_mechanisms.clinical_meaning: Microbial burden and inflammatory cells enter amniotic fluid, causing abnormal amniotic fluid Gram stain, culture, leukocyte esterase, WBC count, low glucose, odor, and fetal exposure.

latent_mechanisms.display_name: 母体全身炎症反応 / Maternal systemic inflammatory response
latent_mechanisms.clinical_meaning: Maternal cytokine release and bacteremia risk drive fever, tachycardia, leukocytosis or leukopenia, CRP/procalcitonin elevation, hypotension, lactate elevation, and sepsis complications.

latent_mechanisms.display_name: 胎児炎症反応 / Fetal inflammatory response
latent_mechanisms.clinical_meaning: Fetal inflammatory response ranges from absent to fetal distress or demise in severe second-trimester infection.

latent_mechanisms.display_name: 卵膜脆弱化・陣痛活性化 / Membrane weakening and labor activation
latent_mechanisms.clinical_meaning: Chorioamnionitis often coexists with or drives PPROM, oligohydramnios, cervical change, and preterm labor over days to weeks.

latent_mechanisms.display_name: 分娩後子宮・骨盤感染進展 / Postdelivery uterine and pelvic infectious extension
latent_mechanisms.clinical_meaning: Residual infected decidua, operative wounds, devitalized tissue, bacteremia, or inadequate anaerobic coverage can persist after birth as endometritis, pelvic abscess, wound infection, atony, postpartum hemorrhage, or maternal sepsis.

latent_mechanisms.display_name: 抗菌薬・分娩ソースコントロール不足 / Inadequate antimicrobial or delivery source control
latent_mechanisms.clinical_meaning: Inactive antibiotics, delayed treatment, undelivered infected intrauterine compartment, cesarean without anaerobic coverage, or persistent postpartum focus sustains maternal and fetal inflammatory hazards.

axes.required_context_rationale: This disease manifold requires active pregnancy or postpartum/peripartum context; without that context, nonspecific abdominal pain, hypertension, hemolysis, liver injury, fever, or shock should not make it rank high.

Fetal demise is a severe but optional fetal consequence of intra-amniotic infection, especially in early gestation.
Vaginal fluid leakage is the observed clinical expression of ruptured membranes or PPROM.
When chorioamnionitis is tied to PPROM, amniotic fluid can be markedly reduced; intact-membrane cases may remain normal.

supportive_care.description: Track maternal temperature, heart rate, blood pressure/MAP, respiratory status, urine output, lactate, CBC, renal function, coagulation, and escalation needs.
Monitor fetal heart rate pattern, fetal tachycardia, variability, decelerations, and response to maternal fever control and resuscitation.
Obtain blood, genital tract, placental, or amniotic cultures when clinically available, but do not delay antimicrobial therapy in suspected infection or sepsis.
Use GBS status, local resistance, culture data, allergy severity, renal function, and postpartum route to maintain active maternal and neonatal coverage.
Reassess delivery route using obstetric indications, maternal stability, fetal status, cervical progress, gestational age, and resource availability rather than infection label alone.
After delivery, reassess fever, uterine tenderness, lochia, wound status, bacteremia, endometritis, pelvic abscess, and need for continued antibiotics.
Because infection increases atony risk, prepare uterotonics, quantified blood loss, blood products, and coagulopathy management as clinically indicated.
Communicate maternal fever, timing of antibiotics, rupture duration, GBS/pathogen context, fetal tracing, gestational age, and cultures to the neonatal team.

quality_notes: Semantic clinical ranking labels are intentionally absent; treatment selection is left to forward simulation and outcome/RMST under context axes.
Exactly one derived_hazard axis is present: mortality_hazard_in_D-CHORIOAMNIONITIS.
Fetal, neonatal, preterm, postpartum, DIC, ARDS, AKI, atony, hemorrhage, abscess, and septic shock risks are event_hazard axes, not additional mortality outcomes.

Rupture duration, GBS/pathogen context, epidural fever, delivery route, gestational age, antibiotic coverage, and neonatal resources are modifiers or observed axes rather than disease-name qualifiers.
No real case reports or disease-specific case JSONs were searched, read, or used for this disease-only distillation.
